reply_text:
*I’d hold the merge.* Reviewed `http-retries` (`b04b610`) against `main` (`5f9be03`). Four findings:

1. *[P1] `timeoutMs: 0` no longer disables timeouts* — `src/http.js:11`  
   The switch from `??` to `||` converts an explicit zero into the 10-second default. This breaks the documented contract and the existing nightly-export caller in `src/export.js:4`. Confirmed with an export reproduction using an accelerated timer. Restore nullish defaulting and add a zero-timeout regression test.

2. *[P1] Retries silently replay non-idempotent requests* — `src/http.js:30–33`  
   The loop retries every method by default, including POST. A server can commit a mutation and still return 503; replaying it can duplicate the operation. A local-server reproduction received the identical POST twice. Automatic retries should be limited to safe/idempotent operations, with explicit opt-in or an idempotency guarantee for mutations.

3. *[P2] Stream request bodies cannot be replayed* — `src/http.js:31`  
   Each attempt reuses the same `init.body`. Native fetch consumes a `ReadableStream` on the first attempt, so a retry throws instead of making another request. Confirmed: a POST receiving 503 failed on attempt two with `TypeError: Response body object should not be disturbed or locked`. Require a fresh-body factory or avoid retrying non-replayable bodies.

4. *[P2] Discarded response bodies are never released* — `src/http.js:32–33`  
   Retryable responses are abandoned without consuming or cancelling their bodies. With real fetch responses, this can retain connections/resources and exhaust bounded connection pools under sustained failures. Confirmed that neither discarded body was cancelled in a two-retry reproduction. Release each response before waiting/retrying.

*Validation:* All three existing tests pass, but they don’t cover these cases; the retry tests use bodyless response stubs. I ran additional in-memory/local-server reproductions only. No files were changed, and the working tree remains clean.
